title: Term 3 and 4 Examination
instructions: This paper covers the work of Terms 3 and 4.
This question paper consists of 4 questions. Answer ALL the questions.
Read each question carefully before you answer it.

sections.title: QUESTION 1: 1960: Sharpeville and the Armed Struggle
sections.instructions: Read the text below, then answer the questions.

context.title: Source I: A survivor's account (a composite based on survivors' testimonies)
context.text: We were singing and some were laughing. Nobody had a weapon. Then the shooting started and people began to fall. We ran, but the bullets were following us. I saw a woman fall next to me; she was shot in the back.

context.title: Source J: A police commander's view (a composite based on police statements to the press in 1960)
context.text: The native mentality does not allow them to gather for a peaceful demonstration. For them to gather means violence. My men were in danger and had to defend themselves.

context.title: Source K: From Nelson Mandela's statement at the Rivonia Trial, 20 April 1964
context.text: I have fought against white domination, and I have fought against black domination. I have cherished the ideal of a democratic and free society in which all persons live together in harmony and with equal opportunities. It is an ideal which I hope to live for and to achieve. But if needs be, it is an ideal for which I am prepared to die.

questions.prompt: Who led the PAC when it was formed in 1959?
On which date did the Sharpeville massacre take place?
How many people were killed at Sharpeville?
What was the name of the ANC's armed wing formed in 1961?
The ANC and PAC were banned after the Sharpeville massacre.
21 March is commemorated today as…
Compare Sources I and J. (a) How do they differ about the crowd? (b) Which source is more reliable? Give TWO reasons.
questions.memo:
(a) ✓ Source I says the crowd was peaceful and unarmed; Source J claims they were violent and the police were in danger (1)
(b) ✓ Source I is more reliable (1)
✓ Evidence that most were shot in the back supports it (1)
✓ The commander wanted to justify the police and shows racist bias (1)

questions.prompt: Read Source K. What kind of society did Mandela want?
questions.memo:
✓ A democratic and free society (1)
✓ where all people live in harmony with equal opportunities, without white or black domination (1)

context.text: IF WE MUST DO AFRIKAANS, VORSTER MUST DO ZULU
